guard: a branch that loses a race stops parking NOW and its recorded cancellation is DISCHARGED — the pause claimed, the consumer deleted, the class carried across the engine bridge, and `cancel.issued` flipped true only after the world was swept
why: THE DEFECT WAS REPRODUCED LIVE THROUGH THE REAL BINARY BEFORE ANY OF THIS EXISTED (#532). A
race of two channel waits, decided by one published message: the run hung forever after the
decision (killed at 20s+, still parked), the loser's durable consumer stayed live on the
broker, and the completed-run journal carried `cancel: { losers, issued: false }` that nothing
in the tree ever flipped or acted on. Two separate halves, separately breakable:
THE HANDLER HALF — MeshHandler ignored `ctx.signal` in all three pause kinds, so a cancelled
branch parked to its own deadline (or forever, with none) while the scope's `allSettled`
waited on it. The cancellation now ends a `wait` on its poll cadence and a `sleep`/`checkpoint`
through a contender in the settle race, claiming the pause so the armed schedule cannot fire
into a branch that is over. And the class must SURVIVE THE ENGINE BRIDGE: thrown on the host
side of the port and flattened to a plain Error, it settled the loser `failed (L4000)` — the
journal recording a failure the program never had. Measured with the message reading
`cancelled: a sibling branch won the race` inside a handler-fault, which is the flattening in
one line.
THE DISCHARGE HALF — `issued` is the record's promise that the world was swept, and the driver
is who keeps it: at completion, each un-issued scope's loser subtrees go to the handler's
`discharge` (claim timers, delete consumers, idempotent), and only then is the entry
re-appended with `issued: true`. The dirty-loser block is the ONLY thing grading the world
half, because the live path cleans up after itself and a suite that only drove the live path
would call the sweep proven while it swept nothing.
THE TWO BRIDGE MUTANTS REBUILD `@cotal-ai/lang` IN THEIR COMMAND: the v2 engine's worker runs
the compiled artifact, so a source mutation in bridge.ts is invisible to the suite until dist
is rebuilt. Their commands rebuild before the suite; after the proof, rebuild once by hand
(`pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/lang build`) because the tool's restore verifies source, not dist.

mutations.name: the wait loop never looks at its signal, so a cancelled wait parks to its timeout
mutations.expectRed: the cancelled wait did not end within 10000ms
mutations.cell: the cancelled wait did not end within 10000ms
mutations.note: The shipped defect's wait half, restored one condition wide. Measured 2026-09-02 before this entry was written: block 11's deadline cell reds first, followed by the consumer and claim cells, then block 12's whole discharge chain — the loser's 10m timeout outlives every deadline the suite carries, which is the hang that was reproduced live wearing a bound so it grades red rather than inconclusive.

mutations.name: the settle race has no cancel contender, so a cancelled sleep parks to its deadline
mutations.expectRed: the cancelled sleep did not end within 10000ms
mutations.cell: the cancelled sleep did not end within 10000ms
mutations.note: The same law at the other park — `sleep` and `checkpoint` share settle(), so one contender serves both and one deletion breaks both. Measured 2026-09-02: mesh-sleep block 4 reds on its deadline cell, then on the claim cell; 18 passed, 3 failed, nothing upstream disturbed.

mutations.name: the driver never sweeps, so a completed run's recorded cancellation stays un-issued
mutations.expectRed: the recorded cancellation is DISCHARGED: `issued` reads true off the journal once the world is quiet
mutations.cell: the recorded cancellation is DISCHARGED: `issued` reads true off the journal once the world is quiet
mutations.note: The whole second half of #532 deleted at its one call site. Measured 2026-09-02: block 12's issued cell reds first with `{losers:["slow"],issued:false}` — the exact bytes every completed run in the tree carried before the sweep existed — then block 13's consumer and record cells. The runs still complete, which is why nothing upstream of the discharge cells notices.

mutations.name: adoption never re-issues, so recovery waits for completion to sweep a dead loser
mutations.expectRed: the adoption sweep ends the dead loser's world state and flips the record WHILE the run is still parked
mutations.cell: the adoption sweep ends the dead loser's world state and flips the record WHILE the run is still parked
mutations.note: The adoption-time call, deletable separately from the completion sweep: a takeover of a run parked past its race decision must re-issue the recorded cancellation BEFORE any new step, or the dead loser's consumer and pause outlive the crash for as long as the run keeps running. Measured 2026-09-03: exactly one cell red — block 14's WHILE-parked cell reads issued:false with the consumer still live — and the block's completes cell stays green because the completion sweep still fires at the end, which is precisely the discrimination the cell exists to grade; 53 passed, 1 failed.

mutations.name: the sweep flips the record without sweeping the world
mutations.expectRed: the consumer the dead loser left behind is deleted by the discharge, not by anyone's live cleanup
mutations.cell: the consumer the dead loser left behind is deleted by the discharge, not by anyone's live cleanup
mutations.note: The lie the flip exists to prevent: `issued: true` over a consumer nobody deleted. Measured 2026-09-02: exactly ONE cell reds — block 13's consumer cell — and 50 pass, because the live path cleans up after itself everywhere else. The dirty-loser block is the only thing in the tree that grades the world half, which is precisely why it drives a handler that dies without cleaning.

mutations.name: the bridge flattens a cancellation on the way out, so a bridged loser settles failed
mutations.expectRed: the losing wait settled `cancelled` — the class crossed the engine bridge instead of flattening to a fault
mutations.cell: the losing wait settled `cancelled` — the class crossed the engine bridge instead of flattening to a fault
mutations.note: The host-side half of the crossing. Measured 2026-09-02 (after `pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/lang build`, which the command does first — the v2 worker runs the compiled artifact): one cell reds, with the journal showing `failed`/`L4000` whose message is `cancelled: a sibling branch won the race` — the class loss in a single record. The run still completes because a failed loser is out-clocked by the winner, which is why only this cell notices.
